cover.title: the founder who ships before ready

inner.title: ship it embarrassed
inner.body: reid hoffman's rule: if you're not embarrassed by your first version, you launched too late. the polish you're adding is mostly for your ego.
inner.label: ship the cringe

inner.title: timebox the spec
inner.body: yc's michael seibel says if you launch in three weeks, build only what fits in three weeks. skip that and three weeks becomes three months.
inner.label: cut it anyway

inner.title: announce the date
inner.body: pick a launch day and post the headline publicly before the product ships. a private deadline is just a suggestion you keep renegotiating.
inner.label: no take-backs

inner.title: build the audience first
inner.body: by september 2024, product hunt featured only about 10% of launches, per tetriz.io data. launch day reveals your audience, it doesn't create one.
inner.label: 90% unseen

inner.title: launch to start
inner.body: paul graham wrote that you haven't really started working on your product until you've launched. everything before launch day is guessing.
inner.label: day zero

closer.HEADLINE:
ready is a date,
not a feeling.
closer.CTA: comment launch and we'll reply with the full guide
